title: Automated spike attribution & runbook generator for usage/cost/latency anomalies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our console alerts fire frequently for usage, cost, and latency spikes but triage is slow and noisy. On-call engineers and customers spend significant time manually correlating signals (token counts, model variants, region routing, batching changes, recent deployments) to determine root cause. False positives from transient load patterns reduce trust in alerts.

Goal: Build an automated spike attribution engine that turns raw anomaly events into prioritized action items and a starter runbook. The system should: 1) correlate across metrics (requests/sec, tokens, p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, cost by customer/model/route), 2) produce ranked root-cause hypotheses with confidence scores, 3) auto-populate a runbook template with suggested checks and mitigation steps, and 4) attach relevant artifacts (dashboard links, recent deploy PRs, config diffs) to the alert.

Scope: Backend pipeline + service logic that enriches anomaly events prior to Console alerting flow. UI/console work (rendering runbooks) is out of scope for this ticket but we will emit links/structured metadata for the frontend to render.

High-level approach:
- Ingestion: extend usage analytics pipeline to emit anomaly candidates with context (customer_id, route, model_version, region, batching_profile). Add lightweight event bloom to reduce cardinality explosion.
- Attribution heuristics: combine signal correlation (time-shifted cross-correlation), feature delta scoring (e.g., model_version bump, config change), and causal priors (e.g., region-wide infra issues). Use ensemble scoring to produce ranked hypotheses.
- Runbook generator: map top hypotheses to templated verification steps (e.g., "verify recent deploys for model X", "check KV cache hit rate for prefix Y", "confirm autoscaling group activity"). Provide severity-based suggestions (rate-limit, failover to cheaper model, open support case).
- Artifacts: attach precomputed links — consolidated dashboard query, last 6 deploy PRs touching inference service, recent rollout events, top offending customers list with anonymization flag.
- Output: structured enrichment payload included in alert webhook and stored in the incidents index for postmortem analysis.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for Done):
1) For synthetic spike tests (see test vectors) the attribution pipeline returns the correct top hypothesis in >= 85% of cases across 6 scenarios (deployment-induced latency, bursty tenant, KV-cache thrash, quantization fallback, region outage, misconfigured batching).
2) Each alert produced by the pipeline includes a runbook skeleton with at least 3 validation steps and 2 mitigation suggestions, plus 1 dashboard link.
3) Enrichment payload size <= 64KB and ingestion latency (time between anomaly detection and enriched alert available) <= 12s for <= 1k concurrent anomaly candidates.
4) No PII leaked in attachments; customer identifiers either hashed or redacted according to privacy policy.
5) Feature flagged and gated behind opt-in beta; rollout plan documented.

Implementation notes:
- Use existing materialized timeseries (metrics-store) for quick correlation queries; fall back to raw events in s3 for deeper analysis.
- New schema: anomaly_enrichment_v1 (flat key-value fields and URLs). Keep schema simple to ease Console consumption.
- Prototype attribution model as rules+features in Python service (batch scoring via Beam + real-time scoring in Go microservice).
- Persist hypotheses and runbooks in incidents index (Elasticsearch/Opensearch). Keep TTL for short-lived enrichments (30 days).
- Add an observability dashboard to track attribution precision, enrichment latency, and false-positive rate.

Data considerations:
- For per-customer lists, use hashed_customer_id and provide count/fraction metrics rather than raw request logs.
- Ensure KMS encryption at rest for any stored raw traces used for deep attribution.

Testing plan:
- Generate 6 canonical synthetic scenarios (see test_vectors.md) and run end-to-end pipeline in staging.
- Create chaos test for concurrent anomalies and validate enrichment latency.
- Run privacy verification to ensure no raw keys leak.
- Manual QA: on-call walkthrough with sample alerts and runbook steps.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag off by default. Enable for internal beta orgs (10 customers) -> collect metrics -> expand to opt-in via Console -> auto-enable for customers on Dedicated plan after release.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy or incorrect attributions undermine trust. Mitigation: conservative confidence threshold, show provenance, allow dismiss/feedback to improve models.
- Risk: storage/compute costs for deep correlations. Mitigation: use sampling and approximate statistics for high-cardinality signals.

Notes on incremental deliveries:
- M1 (2 weeks): schema + pipeline hooks + simple rule-based scoring (deploy/version delta, region outage) + single runbook template.
- M2 (3 weeks): add time-shifted correlation, customer-level aggregation, dashboard links.
- M3 (2 weeks): ensemble scoring, canary rollout, metrics and feedback loop.
